doc.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 17, 2022 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Origin of Mama's Licking Stick Clarinet Ensemble
summary: As a child of eight, Harrison was punished by his mother with an hour of clarinet practice; Rowe cites Buddy DeFranco's 'agony stick'.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Right. Well I’m very glad that all the work you’ve done over the years in the 70s and beyond seems to be still something you can build on and that it’s ongoing. And I’d also like to say that you had one of the best band names ever with Mama’s Licking Stick Clarinet Ensemble. I love that.
You know where that came from?

My mother, you know every time — when I was eight years old they gave me the clarinet. Eight years old, okay? So for discipline and punishment, if I’d do something wrong instead of giving me a licking, hitting or spanking, “Play your clarinet for an hour today.” You know. And I would hate that. It was like punishment to me. Sitting in a room with the clarinet, sitting in the room with this thing for an hour? I mean that was something else. That was the most horrible thing. And then I was made to clean up my room and then do homework.
Well you didn’t know that it was going to pay benefits later.
I didn’t know that. You know I was just — all I know was I was being punished.
You know Buddy DeFranco call the clarinet an “agony stick.”

That’s right. I mean to get it to play in tune and keep your hands over the open holes, I mean your fingers over the open holes and stuff like that. And you can’t get a lot of volume out of it. So what you play has to be really interesting. It has to be really interesting to keep attention.
